headline: PM seeks nationwide cooperation to combat Dengue; 15 districts at high risk
summary: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman has launched a three-month nationwide campaign to prevent Dengue and promote cleanliness. He urged public participation, emphasizing collective effort to control the situation, especially with 15 districts identified as high-risk.
details: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman has called for nationwide cooperation to prevent Dengue and maintain cleanliness across the country. He made this appeal while inaugurating a three-month nationwide Dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign at the South Plaza of the Parliament House on Saturday.

The Prime Minister stated that maximum efforts would be made to tackle the Dengue problem for the next three months, from September 12 to December 12. While a 100% solution might not be possible, effective initiatives would be taken to control the situation.

Rahman urged citizens to prioritize personal and societal health, suggesting that dedicating one hour per week to cleanliness could significantly improve the situation. He also called on everyone to refrain from littering, highlighting the role of every citizen in building a clean nation.

He further mentioned that the people of the country demonstrated that change is possible on August 5, 2024, and now it's time to transform the state. Meanwhile, 15 districts, including Dhaka, Khulna, Chattogram, Gazipur, Mymensingh, Pirojpur, Narayanganj, Jhalokati, Cox's Bazar, Sirajganj, Cumilla, Barishal, Bogura, Bandarban, and Patuakhali, are identified as being at high risk of Dengue infection in the coming weeks.

headline_marked: [[Dhaka 3rd most polluted city]] in the world Saturday morning
headline: Dhaka 3rd most polluted city in the world Saturday morning
summary: Dhaka ranked as the third most polluted city globally on Saturday morning, indicating severe air quality issues affecting its residents.
details: On Saturday morning, Dhaka was identified as the third most polluted city globally. This ranking, reported by Dhaka Tribune, highlights a critical decline in the capital's air quality.

The city's Air Quality Index (AQI) likely registered in the 'unhealthy' or 'very unhealthy' category, posing significant health risks to its inhabitants. Prolonged exposure to such pollution can lead to respiratory illnesses and other severe health complications.

Key contributors to Dhaka's severe air pollution include emissions from vehicles, construction dust, industrial activities, and brick kilns, especially during the dry season. These factors combine to create a hazardous environment for daily life.

Experts continuously urge residents to take protective measures, such as wearing masks outdoors and minimizing outdoor activities. Addressing the root causes of pollution requires concerted efforts from authorities and citizens alike.
